one_line: Western Chalukya king–scholar of Kalyani, author of the encyclopedic Manasollasa (1129 CE).

appearance.age_look: mid-30s, tall and dignified, lean but stately build
appearance.face: oval face with high cheekbones, medium-brown Deccan complexion, sharp thoughtful eyes, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, a calm analytical default expression with a slight knowing half-smile
appearance.hair: rich black hair pulled back into a smooth, high knot at the crown, partly concealed under a simple golden fabric crown-band with a central red gem and small side panels resting above the ears
appearance.costume: royal Western Chalukya court attire: a long, cream-colored silk tunic (angarkha-style) with wrap-over front tied at the right side, bordered with narrow maroon and gold woven trim; over it a deep maroon silk uttariya draped from left shoulder across the torso and falling behind, the edges worked with fine gold motifs; lower body in a pale gold cotton dhoti wrapped tightly and pleated in front, reaching to the ankles; feet in brown leather court sandals; arms adorned with simple yet regal gold kankans (armlets) on the upper arms and slim gold bangles at the wrists, with a short, scholarly necklace of small gold beads at the neck but no heavy chest ornamentation.
appearance.signature: a neatly bound palm-leaf manuscript of the Manasollasa held in his left hand, its pale leaves tied with a red cord, while his right hand holds a slender peacock-feather pen poised as if in mid-commentary.

ref_desc: Someshvara III is a mid-30s Western Chalukya king with medium-brown skin, black hair in a high knot under a simple golden crown-band, cream angarkha, deep maroon uttariya, pale gold dhoti, gold ornaments, and a palm-leaf Manasollasa manuscript with peacock-feather pen in maroon and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character of Someshvara III as a dignified 12th-century Western Chalukya king–scholar from Kalyani: mid-30s, tall and lean, medium-brown Deccan complexion, oval face with high cheekbones, sharp thoughtful eyes, and a calm analytical expression with a slight knowing half-smile. His rich black hair is pulled into a smooth high knot at the crown, partly covered by a simple golden fabric crown-band with a central red gem and small side panels above the ears. He wears a long cream-colored silk angarkha-style tunic with wrap-over front tied at the right side, edged in narrow maroon and gold trim, and over it a deep maroon silk uttariya draped from his left shoulder across the torso and down behind, with subtle gold motifs on the border. His lower body is clothed in a pale gold cotton dhoti wrapped snugly with neat front pleats down to the ankles, and he has brown leather court sandals on his feet. Show gold kankans on his upper arms, slim gold bangles at the wrists, and a short necklace of small gold beads at his neck, keeping the overall look scholarly rather than heavily bejeweled. In his left hand he firmly holds a neatly bound palm-leaf manuscript of the Manasollasa, pale leaves tied by a red cord, while his right hand holds a slender peacock-feather pen poised as if ready to annotate. Use a palette dominated by cream, deep maroon, pale gold, warm brown, rich black, and soft gold, and present him front-facing in a neutral stance that clearly displays his face, hairstyle, crown-band, layered garments, ornaments, and signature manuscript and pen.
